physics_goals.quote: BULLKID-DM is an experiment designed for the direct searches of particle dark matter candidates with mass around 1 GeV, or below, and cross-section with nucleons smaller than $10^{-40}$ cm$^2$.
physics_goals.value: Direct search for particle dark matter of mass around 1 GeV or below with nucleon cross sections smaller than 1e-40 cm^2

summary.plain: BULLKID-DM is a planned dark matter experiment that would use about 800 grams of silicon, cut into over 2000 tiny blocks that are each read by a superconducting sensor, to look for dark matter near the proton mass or lighter. The final detector is planned for the Gran Sasso underground laboratory in Italy in 2027.
summary.technical: Planned phonon-mediated kinetic-inductance-detector (KID) array: ~800 g of silicon in ~2300 dice (16 wafers of 100 mm) acting as a fully active, fiducialisable target for dark matter of mass ~1 GeV or below and nucleon cross sections below 1e-40 cm^2; goals threshold <= 200 eV and background 1 down to 0.01 DRU. Roadmap: prototype (20 g, 160 eV, Sapienza, 2023), demonstrator (60 g, 180 sensors; mid-2026 at Sapienza, by end of 2026 at the LNGS cryo-platform), final experiment at the LNGS cryo-platform in 2027.
